subject: On-prem deployment: operator certification, license boundary and order form coordination
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@medsphere.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsphere.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify license boundary and operator access for on-prem deployment

Evelyn — thanks for the call this morning. Internal stakeholders here want a short, written summary of two items before we move the order form to signatures: 1) what exactly we are licensing for the on-prem installation (runtime vs. code + operator tooling) and 2) what level of operator access Redwood needs during normal support and for an audit/witnessing event.

We attached the updated order form with quantities. Procurement is asking whether the \"Operator console\" reference in Exhibit B implies any software residency rights or elevated administrative accounts on our hosts. Also, our CISO (cc'd) will require SOC2 evidence and a short runbook for temporary witness access. Please confirm next steps and a target timeline — we are aiming to complete commercial signoff by 11/12.

Thanks,
Hannah Li
Director, Cloud Integrations
MedSphere Health

Attachments referenced: MedSphere_OrderForm_v2.pdf
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@medsphere.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify license boundary and operator access for on-prem deployment

Hi Hannah — great speaking earlier. Short answers up front, more detail below:

- License boundary: Redwood licenses the runtime and the server-side inference binaries (the \"Runtime\") and grants MedSphere the right to run that Runtime within your on-prem environment per the Order Form and Exhibit B. Customers do not receive Redwood source code.
- Operator console / operator tooling: The console is a managed operational surface we provide; for Private deployments we offer an on-prem operator image that runs in your environment. By default, we provide administrative accounts scoped to operator actions necessary for support (log collection, deployment updates, health checks). Permanent remote shell-level access to customer hosts is not part of the standard offering; any elevated or resident tooling beyond the standard operator image requires explicit exhibit in the SOW.
- Audit/witnessing: We can support a temporary witness session (time-boxed access and audit trail) or a physical witness at your site. We will provide an attestation runbook and can include a short exhibit describing the scope.

I've looped in Lauren (commercial/legal PM) and Sean (solutions/ops) to help with the order form redlines and the runbook. Rishi, could you propose the minimal addendum language for operator access and a short exhibit for witness sessions? Hannah — we will draft and return redlines by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, sean.gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify license boundary and operator access for on-prem deployment — proposed redlines

Hannah / team — attaching proposed language and a short exhibit for witness sessions. Summary of key points in the redline (see attached MSA_PrivateDeploy_Addendum_redlines.docx):

1) License scope: we propose a clause that the license covers execution of the Runtime, ancillary orchestration images provided by Redwood, and the operator console binaries. No transfer of source code or IP. Limited copy rights for backup/DR (one archival copy).
2) Operator access: default: scoped operator accounts with role-based controls for support engineers; all access requires prior ticketing and is logged. Temporary remote access for troubleshooting or witnessing will be time-boxed (maximum 72 hours per request unless otherwise agreed) and requires a joint access plan with both parties.
3) Witnessing / audit: we propose three options in the exhibit — (A) remote video witness + shared logs, (B) in-person witness with scoped observation and no host shell access, (C) Redwood-provided witness runbook plus signed attestation. Pricing for (B) will be separately quoted.
4) Evidence: per your ask, we will provide an up-to-date SOC2 Type 2 summary and a sanitized snapshot of our internal runbook for witness procedures under NDA.

Open items for your legal/procurement to confirm: whether MedSphere requires permanent operator accounts with sudo-like privileges for vendor personnel (we expect not), and whether you need any on-host resident tooling beyond the provided operator image.

Attachments: MSA_PrivateDeploy_Addendum_redlines.docx

If this draft is acceptable in principle, Lauren and I can circulate a clean addendum and a short exhibit to attach to the Order Form.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: MedSphere Legal <legal@medsphere.com>
To: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsphere.com>, Marco Vasquez <mvasquez@medsphere.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify license boundary and operator access for on-prem deployment — MedSphere comments

Rishi / Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few high-level responses from our side and a couple of redlines attached. Key asks: 

- We cannot accept any language that allows remote maintenance beyond a documented, signed access plan. Please include explicit approval steps and a minimum 48-hour notice for remote access unless we mutually agree otherwise.
- We would prefer permanent operator roles to be scoped and provisioned by MedSphere (vendor accounts can be issued and revoked by us). If Redwood requires the ability to create/delete operator users for upgrades, we need a more detailed justification and compensating controls (MFA, session recording).
- Regarding witness options, we are OK with (A) and (C); we need additional detail for (B) including a non-disclosure procedure for on-site observers and confirmation that no copy of data will be taken. Pricing for option (B) should be visible on the order form.

We are attaching a markup of the addendum and a separate exhibit draft. We will also need the SOC2 Type 2 report (redacted) and the runbook snapshot to move approvals forward. Please confirm whether the SOC2 snapshot can be delivered to our secure share by end of day Friday.

Best,
MedSphere Legal
legal@medsphere.com

Subject: Re: Clarify license boundary and operator access for on-prem deployment — next steps and call

Thanks — all useful. Quick summary and agreed next steps to keep the timeline to 11/12: 

1) Redwood will: 
   - Provide a clean addendum and exhibit incorporating Rishi's language and call out the three witness options with pricing flag for option (B).
   - Deliver SOC2 Type 2 summary and a sanitized witness runbook snapshot to MedSphere's secure share by 2027-11-05 EOD (we will use the Drive folder link above).
   - Update the Order Form to show pricing for in-person witness and include the exhibit reference.

2) MedSphere will: 
   - Confirm whether you want vendor operator accounts to be created/managed by Redwood or provisioned by MedSphere, and indicate preferred control model (target by 11/06).
   - Provide markup comments on the addendum doc sent by our legal team (they already sent a first pass).

3) Logistics: I'll coordinate a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow (11/06) at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the exhibit and access plan. Lauren will send a calendar invite and include Sean to cover technical controls.

If anything changes on timing please flag immediately — we know commercial is on a tight window.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
